questions.stem: For what purpose are Data Rooms normally used?
options: Due diligence of confidential documents, such as business mergers or acquisitions handled by bidders, advisers, and compliance and audit teams
Storing semi-structured and unstructured data for analytics
Running transactional and analytical workloads on one system
Preserving customer history for seven years after account closure
Hosting Hadoop clusters with hundreds of data nodes
questions.explanation: Data Rooms are normally used for due diligence of confidential documents, such as handling business mergers or acquisitions by bidders and advisers, and by compliance and audit teams.

questions.stem: What is the relationship between a Data Room and a Datastore?
options: A Datastore is a small section within a Data Room
They are both the same entity
A Data Room is always physical and a Datastore is always virtual
A Datastore contains only structured data while a Data Room contains only documents
They are unrelated concepts from different disciplines
questions.explanation: Data Rooms and Datastores are described as being both the same entity.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT stated about traditional Physical Data Rooms?
options: They hold physical documents
They are for restricted people only and are secured by guards
Any number of parties may use them simultaneously
A maximum of one or two parties may go in at any given point in time
Multiple teams had to fly over to be near them, which was very expensive
questions.explanation: Physical Data Rooms admit a maximum of one or two parties at any given time, which delays the process when multiple parties need the same room. Simultaneous use by any number of parties is not allowed.

questions.stem: What does VDR stand for in the context of Data Rooms?
options: Verified Document Register
Vendor Due-diligence Report
Volume Data Repository
Virtual Data Room
Validated Data Record
questions.explanation: VDRs, Virtual Data Rooms, came into the picture as a more viable alternative to Physical Data Rooms.

questions.stem: How are Virtual Data Rooms (VDRs) made available?
options: On paper, inside a guarded building
On removable media couriered to each bidder
Through public websites with no login
Only on the seller's local network
Online, behind firewalls and with proper access control
questions.explanation: VDRs are available online, behind firewalls and with proper access control.

questions.stem: How have Virtual Data Rooms changed the bid process?
options: Sellers can invite a bigger audience, and teams in one part of the world can take part in a bid happening in another part of the world
Bidders must now travel to the seller's country to review documents
Only one bidder at a time may access the documents
Documents may now be freely copied and forwarded to advisers
The bid process has become slower but more secure
questions.explanation: VDRs have changed the game: sellers can invite a bigger audience and teams in one part of the world can participate in a bid process happening elsewhere, cutting cost and expediting the process.

questions.stem: Which activities are NOT allowed in a Virtual Data Room, mirroring the rule that nothing may be taken out of a Physical Data Room?
options: Reading and reviewing documents
Copying, forwarding and printing documents
Logging in from another country
Inviting advisers to review documents
Reviewing documents behind a firewall
questions.explanation: Just as individuals in a Physical Data Room may review documents but not take anything out, in a VDR copy, forward and print activities are not allowed.

questions.stem: Why are Virtual Data Rooms still not acceptable in some countries?
options: Because they are too expensive to license
Because firewalls are prohibited by local law
Because the data can be so confidential that a cyber-attack and leakage could result in political instability or similar scenarios
Because bidders in those countries prefer to travel
Because printing documents is mandatory for audits
questions.explanation: In some countries VDRs are still not acceptable because the data is sometimes so confidential that any cyber-attack and leakage could result in political instability or other scenarios.

questions.stem: Which two effects did Virtual Data Rooms have on the due diligence process compared with Physical Data Rooms?
options: Increased cost and slowed the process
Increased cost but expedited the process
Cut cost but slowed the process
Cut cost and expedited the process
Left cost and speed unchanged
questions.explanation: VDRs have cut down the cost and expedited the process.

questions.stem: When the Data Room concept is related to IT projects, what can be called a Data Room?
options: The project's source code repository
The project's test database
The project's Hadoop cluster
The project's email distribution list
The shared drives used for the project's confidential documents
questions.explanation: Although the term is not directly related to the data domain, if it is correlated with an IT project's confidential documents, all the shared drives used for project documents can be called Data Rooms.
